excerpt: I can recall memories [from the non-ownership period of his life] at will. I have normal control over remembering facts and scenes from my past. But when I remember scenes from before the injury, they do not feel as if they happened to me — though intellectually I know that they did — they felt as if they happened to someone else. During the un-owned period I was able to plan for the future.
overview: This evidence constrains overly simple interpretations of R.B.'s deficit. The problem was not a total loss of retrieval control, factual self-knowledge, or future-directed cognition; it was specifically the ownership component attached to pre-injury episodic recollection.
title: Voluntary Recall And Planning
